stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: In a 2019 field study of a coastal dialect, researchers recorded three features that set local speech apart from the regional standard: the dropping of final consonants, as in "han" for "hand"; a merger of vowels in words such as "pin" and "pen," which most speakers pronounce identically______ a habitual "be," used to mark actions that happen repeatedly.
explanation: This sentence lists three features, and the items already contain commas ("pin" and "pen," which...). The first and second items are already separated by a semicolon after "hand." To match that pattern, you also need a semicolon before the final item, so "identically; and" is correct.

A.why: You chose the comma because of the words right around the blank. The list already uses a semicolon between its first two items, though, and the items contain their own commas. A comma here makes it unclear where the second item stops.

C.why: You put a colon in the middle of a list. A colon can introduce a list, and this sentence already has one before "the dropping." A second colon between list items doesn't tell the reader that a new item is starting.

D.why: You ended the sentence early. The words after the period ("And a habitual 'be,' used to mark actions...") have no main verb, so they form a fragment and not a complete sentence.

D.why: You decided from the nearby words alone. The comma before "which" made a comma at the blank look natural. But the sentence already separates its items with a semicolon after "extinct." Using a comma here mixes separators, and the reader can no longer tell where the second item ends.
